synopsis: EMESRT PR-5A provides mining-specific surface vehicle-interaction scenarios and storyboards that can seed a validation scenario catalogue and supply functional performance requirements in the test traceability chain [f4078, f7747, f7106]. Its nine-level control model culminates in Level 9 intervention, where the system takes control from the operator to automatically slow and stop the machine [f4080, f4081, f7744]. The September 2024 update is confirmed, but its revision number remains uncertain: secondary and vendor sources cite Revision 3.0, while EMESRT’s activity report specifies no revision number [f6566, f6565, f7743, f6564]. Reported counts of 24 scenarios and 17 published surface storyboards appear in tension, although Chapter 8 says they count different things [f4079, f6567]. For mining customers, the booklet recommends mapping validation requirements to PR-5A scenarios and MOSH F&TPR numbers, but PR-5A supplies no statistical acceptance target; its scenario content is not machine-readable, covers only expert-envisaged situations and gives no occurrence frequencies [f2645, f324, f13265, f13266, f13267].
